reconcile.connective: Defenders read "none righteous" as denying self-earned, sinless righteousness, while those called righteous are so by imputed righteousness of faith and relatively before men.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who lists the flat "there is none righteous, no, not one" against the texts naming Abel, Noah, Job, Daniel, Lot, Elisabeth and Zacharias as righteous and asks whether there has ever been a righteous person.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Has there ever been a righteous person?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013), skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/righteous.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: that he was a "righteous" person, not by his own righteousness, but by the righteousness of faith he was both heir and preacher of … and this shows that he was not so by the works of the law, but by the righteousness of Christ; because by them no flesh living is justified in the sight of God
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes Noah being called 'righteous' (Gen 7:1) with 'none righteous' by distinguishing self/works righteousness (denied of all) from imputed righteousness of faith.

excerpts.excerpt_text: not that they were without sin, as none are … but they were so in the sight of God; as they were justified by the righteousness of Christ
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly reconciles the two poles for a named-righteous pair (Zacharias/Elisabeth): they were not sinless ('as none are', conceding the 'none righteous' texts) yet righteous before God by imputation.

excerpts.excerpt_text: deliver . . . souls by . . . righteousness-- (Pro 11:4); not the righteousness of works, but that of grace, a truth less clearly understood under the law (Rom 4:3).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: On the named-righteous side (Noah/Daniel/Job, Ezek 14:14), defines their righteousness as grace-righteousness rather than works-righteousness, the same distinction that absorbs the 'none righteous' verses.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Genesis 7:1 and Luke 1:6
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, harmonizing the 'none righteous' verses with the named righteous by distinguishing imputed righteousness of faith from self/works righteousness, and stating the righteous are 'not without sin, as none are.'
